name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network behaviour on social media, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology and its applications across elections, health topics, and information operations. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution, central to vera.ai WP4 and a large share of recent publications.

name: Disinformation Narratives and Information Operations
description: Monitoring and characterizing disinformation narratives and deceptive information campaigns (e.g. war in Ukraine, LGBTQI+ rights, elections, gambling promotion), including the anatomy of 'zombie' and iterative deception operations. Anchored in the PROMPT project and multiple 2025-2026 papers on strategic information operations.

name: Generative AI and Synthetic Media
description: Study of generative AI's role in disinformation, including synthetic visual persuasion, AI-generated content in coordinated campaigns, and the broader transformation of the disinformation landscape by generative technologies. Reflects current teaching (IA Generativa e Media) and recent book chapters/publications.

name: LLMs for Political Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on integrating and validating large language models within human-in-the-loop pipelines for classifying and annotating political discourse and news content, including comparative embedding-model studies. A rapidly growing methodological line with multiple 2024-2025 papers and international collaborations.

name: Platform Data Access and Research Infrastructure
description: Critical examination of social media research APIs, data access regimes, and platform governance shaping academic research, including the transition from CrowdTangle to Meta's Content Library and DSA-era access tools. Connects to the vera.ai/PROMPT toolbuilding work and recent state-of-the-field reports.

name: Political Polarization and Partisanship on Social Media
description: Analysis of partisan communities, affective polarization, cross-partisan versus insular news consumption, and the interplay of social and traditional media in amplifying political extremes. A long-running core theme spanning Italian, German, and Latin American contexts.

name: Italian Election and News Media Coverage
description: Longitudinal mapping of Italian news media political coverage and Facebook/Instagram engagement patterns across national election cycles (2018, 2019, 2022), the founding empirical programme of MINE and source of many flagship datasets and papers.

name: Problematic Health Information Online
description: Study of coordinated circulation of problematic health content and COVID-19 misinformation across countries (India, Nigeria, Italy), including fact-checking acceleration tools and analysis of online gatekeeping by health information sources.

name: Meta Platform Policy and Political Visibility
description: Evaluation of Meta/Facebook platform policies — such as political content reduction and algorithmic governance — and their effects on the visibility of political actors, parties, and journalistic content. Reflects recent 2025-2026 work on Meta's evolving content moderation regime.

name: Cross-National Coordinated Networks
description: Comparative investigation of coordinated social media networks and political information campaigns across countries including Germany, Brazil, Nigeria, and Latin America, extending coordination-detection methods beyond the Italian context.

name: Social TV and Audience Participation
description: Foundational research strand on second-screen practices and Twitter-based audience engagement around television broadcasts, still referenced in recent encyclopedia entries though no longer an active research front.

name: Public and Sociotechnical Approaches to AI Safety Evaluation
description: Papers framing AI safety practices—red-teaming and evaluation—as sociotechnical activities requiring public involvement, labor consideration, and participatory science methods rather than purely technical procedures.

name: Online Radicalization and Extremism Across Platforms
description: Empirical and review studies of how extremist actors (far-right, jihadist) exploit platform affordances, algorithms, and multimodal content to spread and normalize radical ideologies online.

name: Retrospective Essays on Platformization and Social Media's Trajectory
description: Reflective anniversary/position essays diagnosing the current state of social media and platform economies, tracing how platformization, political economy, and scam/extractive logics have reshaped online life over the past decade.

name: Public Attitudes and Labor Experiences with AI
description: Survey- and discourse-based studies of how publics and workers perceive, use, and are shaped by AI systems, including stakeholder discourse, national attitudes, and worker-reported productivity and displacement effects.

name: LLMs and Computational Methods for Research Workflows
description: Methodological papers deploying LLMs or fine-tuned models to augment scholarly tasks such as peer review, qualitative coding, and domain-specific classification, with attention to human-in-the-loop design and evaluation.

name: Message-Based Interventions for Climate Communication and Misinformation Resistance
description: Experimental and review studies testing how framed messages, chatbots, or inoculation techniques shape audience attitudes, resistance to misinformation, and engagement with climate or conspiracy content.

name: Survey Data Quality, Comprehension, and Recruitment
description: Papers examining the methodological foundations of online survey research, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how representative and valid different opt-in sample sources are, and how novel platform-based recruitment strategies (e.g., Facebook ads) can be used and evaluated for reaching hard-to-survey populations.

name: Computational Approaches to Social Network Structure and Community Formation
description: Papers developing or applying computational/graph-based methods to detect, map, and explain emergent structural patterns—communities, practice clusters, and transitive ties—in large-scale online social networks, using techniques such as self-supervised graph embeddings and causal network analysis.

name: Cultural Imaginaries and Framings of Generative AI
description: Papers examining how generative AI is culturally imagined, discursively framed, and theorized as a medium, ranging from newspaper coverage and Silicon Valley community discourse to media-theoretical accounts of AI's distinctive properties as a creative medium.

name: Recalibrating misinformation exposure and harms narratives
description: Papers that use empirical, large-scale, or naturalistic data to challenge alarmist public and scholarly assumptions about the prevalence, exposure patterns, and societal harms of online misinformation, showing that exposure is concentrated among few users, effects are limited, and everyday misinformation is broader and less exotic than commonly assumed.
